Formulation
Family history of migraine (predisposing) plus sudden onset of severe headache with visual sensitivity (precipitating). Persistent pain and functional impairment may perpetuate distress and reduced work capacity. Protective factors include good sleep, willingness to seek care, and absence of significant mental health history.

Mental Health Care Plan Details
(Address each principal problem identified in Clinical Assessment - Section A. Add additional problems as relevant.)

Principal Problem: Persistent severe headache (possible migraine)
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Achieve effective pain relief  
  • Resume normal work duties without interruption
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Confirm headache etiology through neurological and ophthalmic examination  
  • Provide symptomatic relief and review contraceptive suitability
- Actions (Patient):
  • Book in-person appointment as advised  
  • Start prescribed NSAID with food and may use paracetamol concurrently  
  • Monitor headache characteristics and seek urgent care if pain worsens or new symptoms develop
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Arrange face-to-face neurological/ophthalmic examination and blood-pressure check  
  • Prescribe stronger NSAID and advise concurrent paracetamol use  
  • Reassess oral contraceptive appropriateness if migraine with aura confirmed  
  • Provide safety-net instructions (A&E if severe change)

Secondary Problem: Functional impairment due to pain
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Maintain productivity while recovering  
  • Minimize work absences
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Support graded return to full work capacity
- Actions (Patient):
  • Implement regular breaks, adequate hydration, and migraine-friendly environment (low light)  
  • Communicate work limitations to employer as needed
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Issue medical certificate if required  
  • Provide employer-focused guidance upon request

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Possible migraine diagnosis, medication use, pill-related considerations, when to seek emergency care
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Intensifying pain, changes in vision, nausea/vomiting, new neurological deficits, nocturnal awakening with pain
- Coping Strategies: Medication adherence, rest in low-light environment, hydration, timely medical review
